observed_statement_hints.exact: BES does not solve power problems by pooling data; if most individual studies are underpowered, aggregating them can strengthen support for the null or unconstrained alternative.
BES behaves similarly to meta-analysis in many settings: support for the correct hypothesis increases with larger sample sizes and more studies.
It does not behave like data pooling: adding more underpowered studies can amplify support for an alternative rather than rescue a true but weakly supported hypothesis.

context.rationale: The current proposition bundles two distinct claims: BES can behave similarly to meta-analysis in some settings, but BES is not data pooling and can diverge when studies are underpowered or boundary-adjacent. The mixed asserted/negated literature annotations are therefore better handled by resynthesizing the proposition into narrower condition-aware claims than by treating the negated annotations as simple disputes of one stable proposition.

new_propositions.body: Bayesian Evidence Synthesis can behave similarly to meta-analysis in settings where study evidence is informative: support for a correct hypothesis tends to increase with larger samples and more studies.

frontmatter.object: meta-analysis-like accumulation of support under informative study evidence
frontmatter.subject: Bayesian Evidence Synthesis

new_propositions.title: BES behaves like meta-analysis when study evidence is informative

new_propositions.body: Bayesian Evidence Synthesis is not data pooling: when individual studies are underpowered, adding more such studies can strengthen support for the null or an unconstrained alternative rather than rescue a weak true hypothesis.
new_propositions.title: BES does not rescue underpowered studies by pooling data

notes: Resynthesizes the broad BES/meta-analysis proposition into a positive similarity claim and a negative non-pooling/underpowered-study claim.
